title: Composite tool workflow safety and output schema
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a pluggable composite tool execution workflow that supports multi-tool chaining, deterministic result injection, streaming-compatible structured outputs, and robust recursion/loop guards. This ticket covers runtime changes (executor orchestration), API compatibility layer to support legacy tool contracts, schema for structured outputs (stable JSON envelopes), and telemetry/guardrails to detect and mitigate recursion loops during live streams. Deliverables: design doc, reference implementation in the runtime, unit + e2e tests, migration guide for existing tools, and rollout plan with canary metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published and reviewed: RFC linked with architecture diagrams and sequence flows
Executor can chain a sequence of heterogeneous tools in a single request with deterministic result injection semantics (no race conditions across injected results)
Streaming responses remain live while tools execute; partial structured envelopes emitted to clients with stable schema version header
Recursion/loop detection triggers a safe halt and fallback policy within < 500ms of detection for 99% of test cases
Compatibility layer supports existing tool contract v1 and new contract v2 mapped via adapters; no customer-facing breakage in staged rollout
Automated tests cover: unit harness for loop detector, integration tests for multi-tool chains, and stress tests for 500 concurrent chains achieving target p95 latency
Telemetry surfaces: per-call tool-chain depth, injection events, loop-detection alerts, and false-positive rate <= 0.5% after tuning
Canary rollout plan documented and validated with traffic-shift experiments and rollback hooks
discussion: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after spike showed non-determinism when multiple tools injected results concurrently into a streaming response. Initial hypothesis: missing ordering guarantees and ambiguous injection contract.

2026-02-22: Architecture RFC drafted (confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUN/pages/TOOL-EXEC-RFC). Proposed approach: named injection slots + monotonic injection tokens + stream envelope versioning.

2026-02-25: Eng sync. Trade-off: strict ordering (simpler correctness) vs optimistic parallelism (better latency). Decided to start with ordered injection with async optimization path behind feature flag.

2026-02-28: Prototype implemented in runtime branch refactor/tool-exec-composite (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218). Prototype demonstrates deterministic injection for 3-tool chain and emits structured envelopes on stream.

2026-03-03: Design review feedback from Product and DX: require stable JSON envelope schema and explicit schema_version header in every stream chunk. Added acceptance criteria for schema stability and migration notes.

2026-03-05: Security review requested due to tool output injection into user-visible stream. Scoped threat model: malicious tool supplying control fields in envelope. Mitigation: runtime sanitization + allowlist of injection keys. Security review started (ticket SE-1792).

2026-03-08: Performance tests: ordered injection shows 8-12% p95 latency regression under high-concurrency compared to baseline. Proposed mitigations: batching injection tokens and opportunistic parallel injection for non-dependent tools (feature-flagged).
2026-03-10: PM requested compatibility layer to support existing tool contracts (v1) for customers on Dedicated. Implemented adapter shim and compatibility tests; documented mapping in confluence.

2026-03-12: Current status: core executor changes implemented; loop detector unit tests passing. Integration tests failing intermittently in stress suite (investigating flakiness related to backpressure and stream ordering).
notes_for_oncall: If loop-detection alerts spike during canary, immediately scale fallback route that truncates tool chains to safe depth and enable synchronous-only injection mode. Alert thresholds: rate > 5/min for errors or loop-detections leading to client-visible truncation.
